slides.title: Sports and Health
bullets: Prepare to read, discuss and write
slides.narration: Welcome to Grade 6 English, Unit 2: Sports and Health. Unit 2 pairs an information text on the science of sport and health with the environmental story 'When the Leaves Stop Speaking', in which a young researcher named Amal fights to protect a drying forest. You will study twenty-eight precise words such as ecosystem, transpiration, efficient, propaganda and restoration, and you will master the First Conditional, including 'unless' and modal verbs. You will separate fact from opinion, then write a biography, a sports commentary and persuasive pieces of your own. In this short lecture, preview the key ideas and prepare for the independent lesson.

slides.title: What you will achieve
bullets: Use and understand 28 new vocabulary words linked to science, the environment and health
Identify and use the First Conditional to talk about likely future events and their results
Use 'unless' and modal verbs to shape conditional sentences
slides.narration: By the end of this unit, you will be able to use and understand 28 new vocabulary words linked to science, the environment and health. You will also identify and use the First Conditional to talk about likely future events and their results. You will also use 'unless' and modal verbs to shape conditional sentences. Keep these goals in mind as you work.

slides.title: Language for precise thinking
slides.narration: Your vocabulary work begins with these words: awkward, bargain, bruise, controversy, correspondingly, evidently. Listen to each pronunciation in the vocabulary lab, study its meaning in context, and use the word accurately in your own discussion and writing.

slides.title: Read critically
bullets: Training Champions: The Science Behind Sport
Reading Closely: Fact and Opinion in Health Writing
slides.narration: The reading sequence includes Training Champions: The Science Behind Sport and Reading Closely: Fact and Opinion in Health Writing. Read actively. Identify each text's central ideas, notice viewpoint and reliability, and support every inference with relevant evidence from the text.

slides.narration: The first language focus is What Is the First Conditional? The First Conditional describes real, likely situations in the future and the result that will follow. We use it when there is a genuine chance that the condition will happen. Notice the structure in the model examples, then apply it deliberately in connected sentences and paragraphs.

slides.title: Use English for a real purpose
bullets: Explain, support and improve your ideas
slides.narration: In speaking, you will complete Speaking 1: Sports Interview Role-Play. Organise your ideas, use evidence and respond clearly to questions. In writing, you will plan, draft, check and revise. Use the success criteria before submitting your work.

slides.title: You are ready to begin
bullets: Activities, quiz and optional live sessions
slides.narration: You are ready to begin. Start with the vocabulary lab, continue through reading and comprehension, apply the grammar focus, and complete the speaking and writing practices. Use the AI tutor for hints and feedback any time, and bring your questions to a live session too if you join one.
